purpose: Pre-inference heuristic overlap screen; no detector predictions or labels were used.

algorithm.name: 63-bit perceptual DCT hash
algorithm.distance: Hamming distance; smaller is more similar
algorithm.selection: three nearest training images for every pilot frame, irrespective of distance

visual_review.coverage: All 36 pilot frames paired with their single nearest training candidate were inspected across three contact sheets. Second and third nearest candidates are recorded but were not individually inspected.
visual_review.reviewer: Codex subagent visual inspection; not an independent human review
visual_review.finding: No obvious duplicate image or same-scene match was observed among the 36 reviewed nearest pairs.

by_source.arrival: 12 pairs reviewed. Pilot shows a pavement with blue footprints; nearest candidates show different people, objects and settings.
by_source.scissors: 12 pairs reviewed. Pilot shows hands cutting cardstock; nearest candidates show different people, tools or weapon compositions.
by_source.steak: 12 pairs reviewed. Pilot shows steak cutting on a board; nearest candidates show different people or object arrangements. The candidate featuring blades on a wooden background is a visibly different scene.

visual_review.conclusion_limit: The heuristic and this candidate review did not reveal overlap; they cannot establish that the source recordings are absent from all training or pretrained data.

limitations: Perceptual hash is a candidate-screening heuristic, not proof of source independence.
Crops, rotation, perspective, changed backgrounds and different frames from one recording may evade it.
Only the selected 3267 fine-tuning training images were searched; validation, test, excluded raw data and general pretrained data were not searched.
Visually similar compositions may produce close hashes without being the same image or scene. No universal match threshold is asserted.
